purpose: Canonical, engine-neutral workload for the Strata-comparable Qwen4Exp baseline (roadmap A6). tools/qwen4exp_benchmark_replay.py builds each engine's exact command line from this spec so a single feature toggle changes exactly one variable. Diagnostic only: the production loader gate stays closed and ESE Qwen4Exp output logits are not yet verified.
notes: Measured 2026-10-05: this shard holds 27,394 MiB of repeating-layer tensors (48 layers) plus a 510 MiB output layer; the 28.8 GB second shard is entirely the per_layer_token_embd PLE table and is not a resident model tensor. Row 'Memory required for model tensors + cache: 29750 MiB' versus 'Memory available on all devices - compute: 14854 MiB' for CUDA0+CUDA2: a full (-ngl 99, no MoE placement flag) offload cannot fit two 8/10 GiB cards and dies in ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer (14254.41 MiB on device 0).

ese.moe_placement=cpu therefore adds --cpu-moe: the ~24.3 GiB of expert tensors stay in host RAM (CUDA_Host buffer 24303 MiB) while 1867 MiB + 2056 MiB of dense weights land on CUDA0/CUDA2. Adaptive expert GPU residency (separate VRAM cache) is roadmap D1, so the baseline deliberately runs with expert_vram_cache_mib=0 rather than mixing an optimization into the baseline.
Devices CUDA0+CUDA2 match the Strata slot config (gpu [0,2]) so both engines select the same physical cards (18 GiB nominal combined VRAM, less available at runtime).

phase=prefill records prompt-eval cost (n_predict 1); phase=decode records steady-state decode (n_predict 128). mtp=on is only valid for Strata; the harness refuses it for ESE (no MTP/speculative path). kv_policy=resident means full GPU KV for ESE versus a bounded GPU window with host backing for Strata; these are not identical policies. kv_policy=host adds -nkvo for ESE and is explicitly unsupported for Strata: dropping --kv-resident makes Strata fully GPU-resident, not host-only. ESE has no bounded GPU-resident KV window yet (roadmap D2).

The Strata toggles are applied by writing a config derived from strata.config and launching serve/server.py directly with it (strata.python + strata.server + --port strata.benchmark_port). The launcher wrapper strata_service.sh always reads the on-disk config, so it cannot express a toggle; the benchmark never edits the on-disk config or runs while the launcher slot is up.
